absent: Full field layout of managed area and range descriptors beyond observed uses
Semantics of bitmap size and alignment helpers used during allocation
Guarantees of backing contiguous allocation and migration primitives
Valid values and initialization timing for block order and granularity
Iteration order and stability of free physical range enumeration
Effects of trace points and leak ignore annotations
Interaction between area locks and page allocator locking
Compound page and sanitizer tag handling during claim and free
Lifetime and visibility of accounting counters
Node selection policy on builds without NUMA support

findings.text: Reservation error mode can be enabled on an existing area so later failures keep pages reserved.
A reserved physical extent can be registered as a managed area after sanity validation.
A contiguous reservation can be declared for a node with size limit alignment and placement controls.
A total reservation can be satisfied by one extent when possible and otherwise by several extents.
Managed pages can be allocated frozen with explicit count and alignment, optionally as compound or with normal reference handling.
Previously allocated pages can be returned to the manager with success reported by boolean result.
Frozen contiguous ranges can be returned through a common helper that prepares and frees backing pages.
Reservation status of a physical extent can be queried during early boot.
Managed area table has fixed capacity; creation fails when full and removal reverses global page totals.
Registration requires non empty size, prior reservation, initialized block order and minimal alignment of base and size.
Declaration normalizes alignment upward, requires power of two form, aligns geometry and enforces order granularity and limit containment.
Fixed placement rejects spans crossing the low and high memory boundary and rejects already reserved extents.
Dynamic placement avoids constrained low zones when feasible and prefers high memory before low memory.
Scattered fallback uses aligned free extents above the low address space, retaining a bounded set of largest candidates in address order.
Allocation never exceeds current free count and never hands out ranges lacking page structure contiguity.
Success failure and release counters are maintained separately; one build variant provides inert accounting.
Release requires the whole page span to lie inside a single managed range; oversize or foreign spans are rejected.
Frozen freeing separates compound heads from order zero pages and groups consecutive pages by descriptor section.
Candidate ordering uses decreasing size for retention and increasing base for final layout.
Range list insertion preserves caller defined order and handles empty lists correctly.
A per area interrupt disabling spin lock protects free counts, allocation bitmaps and debug reporting.
A per area allocation mutex serializes backing migration after the bitmap claim, allowing the spin lock to be dropped during migration.
Early reservation candidate holds a base address, a size and list linkage.
Managed area records identity, total and free page counts, bitmap granularity, range extents and node affinity.
Static candidate storage bounds how many scattered extents can be considered during fallback.
Reservation moves from slot creation to populated area, unwinding slot and physical reservation on failure.
Allocation moves from candidate search to bitmap claim to backing migration, clearing the claim on failure and retrying on contention.
Release moves from range location to reference dropping to backing free and bitmap clearing with accounting.
Early boot entries create reservations before general allocators are available and report sizes in megabytes.
Contended backing store causes busy retry on another candidate; incompatible spans are skipped with rate limited notice.
Returning pages still referenced triggers a warning; unknown spans fail lookup without side effects.
Freeing walks each frame by address rather than pointer arithmetic and splits chunks by alignment and buddy maximum.
Invalid geometry, exhausted slots and failed physical reservation produce distinct error results with diagnostics.
Error retention mode is identified by a dedicated flag bit on the area.
Table capacity, name capacity and minimal alignment are fixed limits governing reservations.
